newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: PSA Peugeot sees no plant closures.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot sees no plant closures.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet said on Tuesday that none of the nine Peugeot or Citroen plants were at risk of closure.

"There is an imbalance of short-term working at some plants and supplementary production at others... But there is no problem that would put our five Peugeot sites or our four Citroen sites at risk," Calvet told reporters at the Geneva car show.
"That does not mean we won't present job reduction plans in certain fights for certain functions," he said.
He said that as in previous years the group would try to reduce jobs through "the most acceptable measures," such as attrition, early retirements and internal transfers.
He said the group's strategy was revisited a few months ago and based on forecasts that are close to the current forecast.
"Noises in the press that we have one production center too many, if that were the case, I would know it," he said
Referring to Renault's move to streamline production by reducing the number of plants at which each model is assembled, Calvet said.
"Our position is roughly that when production volumes are such that we are certain they would use total capacity, we would go to single model production,"
Calvet said the group had reduced the cost of investment by 10 percent annually over the last three years and aimed for similar reductions over the next three years.
